title: Realization of Very High Mobility InAs Quantum Wells on InP Substrates Through Convex InAlAs Graded Buffer Optimization
authors: Tyler Lindemann, Rojila Ghimire, Alejandro Alcaraz Ramirez, Ahmad Azizimanesh, Sergei Gronin, Ray Kallaher, Michael J. Manfra
abstract: Due to strong spin-orbit coupling, large Landé $g$-factor, and a highly transparent interface, the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in InAs quantum wells provides an ideal platform for the exploration of topological superconductivity in hybrid semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures. Reduction of disorder in the semiconductor remains a primary challenge to the disambiguation of subtle interaction effects. Here we demonstrate very high mobility InAs 2DEGs grown on insulating InP substrates. Utilizing a convex compositional grading profile in an InAlAs metamorphic buffer we demonstrate InAs quantum wells with thickness greater than 10 nm without need of Ga-containing cladding layers. We examine structural and electrical transport properties of these heterostructures. Advances in the design of the metamorphic InAlAs buffer result in low-temperature electron mobility exceeding $1.7\times10^6$ cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$ at 2DEG density $\leq3.2\times10^{11}$ cm$^{-2}$, the highest value yet reported for this material system.
summary: This work reports on the successful realization of high-quality InAs quantum wells on InP substrates by optimizing the metamorphic buffer layer using a convex grading profile. This advanced growth technique significantly reduces structural disorder, leading to the highest reported electron mobility for this material system. The achievement is vital for advancing research into topological superconductivity in semiconductor-superconductor hybrids.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving very high electron mobility in InAs quantum wells (2DEGs) grown on InP substrates, which is critical for exploring topological superconductivity.
main_result: The authors achieved a record low-temperature electron mobility exceeding $1.7 	imes 10^6 	ext{ cm}^2 	ext{ V}^{-1} 	ext{ s}^{-1}$ in a 14 nm InAs QW by optimizing the buffer layer.
method: They utilized Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) to grow the heterostructures, employing a convex compositional grading profile in an InAlAs metamorphic buffer.
model_or_system: The physical system is a semiconductor heterostructure consisting of InAs quantum wells grown on InP substrates, separated by a metamorphic InAlAs graded buffer. The structure is designed to minimize disorder and strain effects.
key_observables: Low-temperature electron mobility ($\mu$), 2DEG density ($n_{2DEG}$), lattice parameters, and strain energy density.
important_parameters: QW thickness ($>10$ nm), 2DEG density ($\leq 3.2 	imes 10^{11} 	ext{ cm}^{-2}$), and the convex grading profile parameters.
main_assumptions: The convex grading profile successfully minimizes misfit and threading dislocations compared to previous linear grading methods.
figures_summary: Figures show the layer stack, Schrödinger-Poisson modeling of confinement, strain energy density vs. buffer parameters, and RSM data confirming strain characterization.
paper_structure: The paper details the structural optimization using the convex grading buffer, followed by characterization of structural and electrical transport properties, culminating in the measurement of record-high electron mobility.
why_interesting: While focused on semiconductor device physics, the ability to engineer material interfaces with extremely low disorder and high carrier mobility is foundational for building quantum devices, including those for topological quantum computation.
